<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1752
 By Hensley

 HOUSE BILL 1732

 By Stinnett

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Section
 37-1-408; Title 49 and Section 68-6-103, relative
 to training.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 5, Part 3, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 49-5-304.

 (a) Due to the considerable amount of training requirements in state law for

 educators, school personnel, and volunteers at LEAs and public charter schools, the

 following is a non-exhaustive, non-binding, informative list of the training requirements

 and opportunities established in state law:

 (1) The following statutes reference annual training:

 (A) Section 49-5-1007 for the teacher code of ethics;

 (B) Section 49-6-321(a) for a full-time employee to receive

 seizure safety and first aid training;

 (C) Section 49-6-805(7) for teachers and other school personnel

 to receive school safety training;

 (D) Section 49-6-815(b)(1)(E) for faculty or staff members

 carrying a handgun on school grounds to receive training in school

 policing;

 (E) Section 49-6-816(d)(1)(D) for employees carrying a concealed

 handgun on school property;

 (F) Section 49-6-1901 for LEA employees to receive suicide

prevention training;

 (G) Section 49-6-2116(b) for transportation supervisors;

 (H) Section 49-6-3601(b)(1) for coaches to complete certain

training on concussion recognition, and other head injuries, and on

sudden cardiac arrest;

 (I) Section 49-6-3601(b)(2)(C) for certain coaches to receive heat

illness and other environmental conditions training;

 (J) Section 49-6-4217(b) for school resource officers to complete

training in school policing;

 (K) Section 49-50-1602(b) for certain school personnel to

administer glucagon and insulin;

 (L) Section 49-50-1602(d)(3) for school nurses to be educated in

diabetes care; and

 (M) Section 49-50-1602(g)(4) for volunteer staff to administer

anti-seizure medication;

(2) The following statutes reference triennial training:

 (A) Section 49-6-819(b) for teachers, administrators, and other

school personnel to receive de-escalation training;

 (B) Section 49-6-1601(b) and Section 37-1-408 for all school

officials and employees working directly with students to complete a child

abuse training program;

 (C) Section 49-6-3004(c)(1)(B) for employees of an LEA who

work directly with students to receive training on the detection,

intervention, prevention, and treatment of human trafficking; and

 (D) Section 49-6-4503(c)(1) for teachers and counselors on the

 employing LEA's policy prohibiting harassment, intimidation, bullying, or

 cyberbullying;

 (3) The following statutes reference trainings that must be completed

before a person may perform certain acts:

 (A) Section 49-50-1603(e) for persons who seek to administer

 medications to treat adrenal insufficiency;

 (B) Sections 49-2-122(c)(3)(E) and 49-2-122(d) for members of a

 cardiac emergency response team and others on the severity of sudden

 cardiac arrest events and AEDs;

 (C) Section 49-2-137(b)(3) for LEA employees on how to use a

 bleeding control kit;

 (D) Section 49-3-114(c)(3) for certain LEAs on how to budget to

 increase student achievement;

 (E) Section 49-6-1103 for science, technology, engineering, and

 mathematics (STEM) leadership training in STEM innovation hubs;

 (F) Section 49-6-1601(c)(2) for child abuse coordinators;

 (G) Section 49-6-2116(b) for transportation supervisors to

 complete a student transportation management training program;

 (H) Section 49-6-2701(c)(1) for threat assessment teams;

 (I) Section 49-6-3601(b)(1)(C) for coaches to receive training in

 cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and the use of an automated

 external defibrillator (AED);

 (J) Section 49-6-4212 for school administrators conducting

 certain searches;

 (K) Section 49-6-4213(h) for principals and teachers authorized to

test students for drugs;

 (L) Section 49-6-4217(b) for school resource officers to

participate in forty (40) hours of basic training in school policing;

 (M) Section 49-6-816(d)(1)(C) for employees of distressed rural

counties to carry a concealed weapon; and

 (N) Section 49-6-2107(g) for school bus drivers to complete a

school bus driver training program; and

(4) The following statutes reference training opportunities:

 (A) Section 49-2-122(j) for school bus drivers to receive training in

CPR, first aid, and AEDs;

 (B) Section 49-1-215 for teachers on attention deficit disorder and

hyperactivity;

 (C) Section 49-1-223 for teachers, athletic coaches, and athletes

to participate in an asthma treatment training;

 (D) Section 49-1-230 for school personnel to participate in

adverse childhood experiences training;

 (E) Section 49-5-414 for certain individuals to receive training to

in emergency first aid and CPR;

 (F) Section 49-6-3601(b)(3) for coaches to annually complete

training in physical conditions and in the use of training equipment;

 (G) Section 49-10-1304(j) for certain individuals to receive

behavior intervention training; and

 (H) Section 49-50-1802(c)(1) for certain individuals to receive

antisemitism awareness training.

 (b) This section does not exempt any individual from having to comply with a

 training requirement established in or pursuant to the laws of this state, nor does it

 repeal or amend any training opportunity, that are not referenced in this section.

<summary>
The bill would add a nonbinding guide to Tennessee law listing training requirements and opportunities for educators, school personnel, and volunteers at local education agencies (LEAs) and public charter schools. It groups the listed training by whether the cited law calls for it annually, every three years, before certain activities, or as an opportunity. Topics include school safety, student health, child abuse, bullying, and transportation. The list would not be exhaustive and would not excuse anyone from other training requirements. The bill would also add references to the guide in the cited training provisions.

The bill would require LEAs and public charter schools to ensure that teachers, administrators, and other school personnel receive de-escalation training within their first year of employment and every three years afterward. They would have to ensure that officials and employees working directly with students complete child abuse training on the same schedule. For that training, employees could take a program identified by the education department or one meeting guidelines set by the department of children's services. Each LEA and charter school would have to report its compliance to the education department.

At the beginning of each school year, LEAs would have to give teachers and school counselors a copy of their bullying and harassment policy and information about its implementation and prevention strategies. LEAs would also have to train teachers and counselors on the policy within their first year of employment and every three years afterward. The education department would have to provide training guidelines and recommend free prevention resources. The bill would take effect July 1, 2026.
</summary>

assessments.rationale: It covers the added references but omits the redesignation of existing language in two provisions.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would require LEAs and public charter schools to ensure that teachers, administrators, and other school personnel receive de-escalation training within their first year of employment and every three years afterward.
assessments.rationale: It omits that the training is created pursuant to § 49-6-819(a).

assessments.summary_quote: They would have to ensure that officials and employees working directly with students complete child abuse training on the same schedule.
assessments.rationale: The preceding sentence supplies the first-year and three-year schedule, but the summary omits the in-service-training specification for employees.

assessments.summary_quote: For that training, employees could take a program identified by the education department or one meeting guidelines set by the department of children's services.
assessments.rationale: It conveys both permitted bases for the child-abuse training program.

assessments.summary_quote: Each LEA and charter school would have to report its compliance to the education department.
assessments.rationale: It conveys the reporting duty and recipient.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would also add references to the guide in the cited training provisions.
assessments.rationale: It conveys the added cross-references in the training provisions.

assessments.summary_quote: At the beginning of each school year, LEAs would have to give teachers and school counselors a copy of their bullying and harassment policy and information about its implementation and prevention strategies.
assessments.rationale: It omits information about strategies to address bullying and harassment when they occur.

assessments.summary_quote: LEAs would also have to train teachers and counselors on the policy within their first year of employment and every three years afterward.
assessments.rationale: It omits training on appropriate procedures for implementing the policy.

assessments.summary_quote: The education department would have to provide training guidelines and recommend free prevention resources.
assessments.rationale: It omits that the recommended bullying- and harassment-prevention resources must be appropriate and available.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would also add references to the guide in the cited training provisions.
assessments.rationale: It conveys the added cross-references in the training provisions.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would take effect July 1, 2026.
